summary: Jonathan Geen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned his doctorate at McMaster University under Phyllis Granoff by 2001 and taught at McMaster University, Butler University, and the University of Rochester.

Jonathan Glover is a philosopher who attended Tonbridge School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (c. 1960–1964). He held a post at King's College London from c. 1998 to 2013 and taught Amber D. Carpenter.

Jonathan Lear (1948–2025) was a philosopher who studied at Yale University (c. 1965–1969), the University of Cambridge (c. 1969–1971), and The Rockefeller University (c. 1973–1978). He held a post at the University of Chicago from c. 1996 to 2025.

Jonathan Mark Kenoyer is a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist educated at Woodstock School and the University of California, Berkeley (c. 1970–1983). Around 1985, he became a professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison.

Jonathan Z. Smith (1938–2017) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Haverford College, Yale Divinity School, and Yale University. He held posts at UC Santa Barbara (c. 1966–1968) and the University of Chicago (c. 1968–2017).

Jong-Nam Choi is a Buddhist studies scholar who attended Shitennoji University and completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg by 1998 under Lambert Schmithausen, also studying with S. A. Srinivasan, Albrecht Wezler, and David Seyfort Ruegg.

Jongcheol Lee is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Seoul National University and completed a PhD at the University of Tokyo in 1994 under Yasunori Ejima. He held posts at the University of Mysore and the Academy of Korean Studies.

Jongmyung Kim works in Buddhist studies, history, and religious studies. He studied at Yonsei University, Seoul National University, and UCLA (MA by 1994, under Robert E. Buswell Jr.), later serving as an associate professor at the Academy of Korean Studies.
Joryu Chiba (1921–2008) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Ryukoku University and served there as a professor from circa 1958 to 1995.

Josef Schick (1859–1944) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Heidelberg University (c. 1890–1896) and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (c. 1896–1926).
Joseph Campbell (1904–1987) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Dartmouth, Columbia, Paris, and Munich. He taught at Canterbury School (1933–1934) and Sarah Lawrence College (1934–1972).
Joseph D. Markowski is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned a Master of Arts at McGill University under G. Victor Sōgen Hori, attested in 2004.

Joseph E. Schwartzberg (1928–2018) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Brooklyn College (c. 1945–1949) and served as a professor of geography at the University of Minnesota from circa 1964 to 2000.

Joseph Goldstein is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who studied at Columbia University (c. 1961–1965). He studied under Anagarika Munindra and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and taught Jon Kabat-Zinn.

Joseph Hackin (1886–1941) was an archaeologist, Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar, and Buddhist studies specialist. Educated in Paris under Sylvain Lévi, he held posts at Musée Guimet, the French Archeological Delegation to Afghanistan, and EPHE.

Joseph John Loizzo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology educated at Amherst College and Harvard University, studying under Robert A. F. Thurman. He founded the Nalanda Institute for Contemplative Science and was a visiting scholar at Columbia University.
Joseph Margolis (1924–2021) was a philosopher who studied at Columbia University from circa 1947 to 1953. He taught Youru Wang and held a post at Temple University from circa 1968 to 2021.

Joseph Marino is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Washington (attested 2017) under doctoral supervisor Richard Salomon and also studied under Collett Cox.
Joseph Mitsuo Kitagawa (1915–1992) studied at Rikkyo University and earned his PhD at the University of Chicago, where he held posts from c. 1951 to 1985 and served as Dean of the Divinity School.

Joseph Prabhu is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He taught at California State University, Los Angeles, and held visiting professorships at United Theological College, UC Santa Barbara, and Bossey Ecumenical Institute.
